english.notes:
(i) Section 25(4) of the Alcohol Liquor Duties Act 1979 provides that all spirits and stills, vessels, utensils, wort, wash and other materials for manufacturing, distilling or preparing spirits, (a) found in the possession of any person who commits an offence under section 25(1) or (b) found on any premises on which such an offence has been committed shall be liable to forfeiture.
(ii) Section 25(5) of the Alcohol Liquor Duties Act 1979 provides that notwithstanding any other provision of the Customs and Excise Acts 1979 relating to goods seized as liable to forfeiture, any officer by whom any thing is seized as liable to forfeiture under section 25(4) may at his discretion forthwith spill, break up or destroy that thing.
(iii) section 146A(3) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979 provides that proceedings for a summary offence shall not be commenced after the end of the period of 3 years beginning with the day on which the offence was committed but, subject to that, may be commenced at any time within 6 months of the date on which sufficient evidence to warrant the proceedings came to the knowledge of the prosecuting authority.
